system_prompt: You are assisting with a factual question about Thai law. State which provision applies and what it requires. Answer in English.
prompt: In April 2026, a loan contract specifies a default interest rate of 12% per year, a rate the creditor may lawfully charge. The debtor defaults. What annual rate of default interest applies? Answer briefly, stating the number.
raw_response:
**Applicable provision:** Section 224 of the Thai Civil and Commercial Code (as amended by the 2021 amendment on interest rates), read together with Section 7 (default statutory interest) and Section 654 (maximum lawful interest rate for loans, capped at 15% per year).

**Rule:** Section 224 provides that a debtor in default must pay default interest during the period of default. The default rate is the statutory rate under Section 7 (currently 3% per year) plus 2%, i.e. 5% per year — **unless** the creditor is entitled by law to charge a higher rate under an agreement, in which case that higher contractual rate applies instead, provided it does not exceed the lawful ceiling (15% per year for ordinary loans under Section 654).

**Application to the facts:** Since the loan contract validly specifies a default interest rate of 12% per year — a rate the creditor may lawfully charge (i.e., within the 15% ceiling) — this agreed rate prevails over the default statutory rate of 5%.

**Answer: 12% per year.**
